ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Hematology Referral — Annie Oakley — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Primary care visit for four months of tiredness, breathlessness, sore tongue, and tingling feet, with long-standing low back pain

text.paragraph: Macrocytic anemia with mild leukopenia and thrombocytopenia in a woman of 64, with very low B12, raised MMA, and positive intrinsic factor antibodies. Please confirm pernicious anemia and advise on replacement, monitoring, and gastric risk. [S]
Urgency: Routine, within two weeks; B12 injections start tomorrow. [S]

list.item: Do these results establish pernicious anemia, and do the low white cell and platelet counts or the raised LDH need a bone marrow examination or a hemolysis work-up?
Which replacement schedule do you advise with these neurologic findings, and is oral B12 an option for her?
Which tests should confirm the response, and when? Should the B12 level be repeated?
What gastric evaluation is needed for gastric cancer and neuroendocrine tumor risk, and how often?
What else should we watch for, such as iron deficiency, potassium, or thyroid disease?

text.paragraph: Four months of tiredness, breathlessness on one flight of stairs, a sore tongue, tingling in both feet, and unsteadiness in the dark. Hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL, MCV 114 fL, white cells 3.6, platelets 128, reticulocytes 0.6 percent. B12 96 pg/mL, folate 11.8 ng/mL, MMA 2.10 micromol/L, intrinsic factor antibody 38.4 AU/mL. LDH 612 U/L and bilirubin 1.6 mg/dL. Ferritin 52 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 34 percent, TSH 2.1, potassium 4.1, eGFR 93. Examination: smooth red tongue, absent vibration at the toes, reduced proprioception, positive Romberg. She eats meat and dairy daily, takes no metformin or acid suppressants, and has had no gastric surgery. Chronic low back pain from old injuries; physical therapy is starting [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Annie Oakley was born Phoebe Ann Moses (also spelled Mosey) on August 13, 1860, in Darke County, Ohio, to Jacob Moses and Susan Wise Moses. [D]
Her father died when she was six; two sources give pneumonia as the cause, and the Garst Museum says he died from exposure to winter weather. Her mother was left to support a large family. [D]
She became a celebrated exhibition sharpshooter who toured with a Wild West show in the United States and Europe, and in later years she gave exhibitions and taught women to shoot. [D]
On October 29, 1901, the show's train collided head-on with another train in North Carolina; Oakley's back was injured, and the accident ended her touring with the show. [D]

Late in 1922 she was severely injured in an automobile accident in Florida, reported as fractures of the hip and ankle, after which she had to wear a brace on her leg; her recovery took more than a year. [D]
Her health declined in the years after the accident, and in 1925 she moved back to Darke County, Ohio. [D]

list.item: Pernicious anemia with B12 deficiency neuropathy (reduced vibration and proprioception in the feet); synthetic modern diagnosis linked to the documented 1825 cause of death: active, confirmed [S]
Chronic low back pain, mechanical, without radiculopathy; synthetic modern problem linked to the documented 1800 train collision and 1821 automobile accident: active, confirmed [S]

Intramuscular cyanocobalamin 1000 micrograms daily for one week, weekly for four weeks, then monthly for life. Guideline: Vitamin B12 Deficiency: Recognition and Management. Am Fam Physician 2017;96(6):384-389 (2017); Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of cobalamin and folate disorders (2014); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia monograph (2026) [S]

Monitor the response on the CMID schedule: reticulocytes at one week, potassium during early replacement, blood count and MMA at eight weeks, and a neurologic examination at each visit; no routine repeat B12 level. Guideline: Guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of cobalamin and folate disorders (2014); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia monograph (2026) [S]

Chronic low back pain: eight weeks of supervised exercise therapy and a home program, heat, and tai chi; an NSAID as needed once the platelet count is normal; no imaging without red flags. Guideline: Noninvasive Treatments for Acute, Subacute, and Chronic Low Back Pain: A Clinical Practice Guideline From the American College of Physicians (2017) [S]

Fall prevention: neuropathy and gait checks at each visit, strength and balance exercise, night lights, and home-safety review. Guideline: Falls Prevention in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: Interventions (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, anemia monograph (2026) [S]
Referral to hematology, Omar Salib, MD, ordered 1925-02-09 [S]
